messages:
Maya: Flying red-eye to EuroConf next week. Debating seat — aisle for bathroom access or window to sleep? Any must-pack/tips for actually sleeping on overnight flights? :airplane:

Sam: Aisle if you need to get up a lot, but bring big noise-cancelling earbuds + eye mask. Melatonin helps me. Also compression socks.

Jonah: Window all the way — you can lean, no one climbing over you. Neck pillow + hoodie hood = miracle. Also try to reserve bulkhead/exit row for extra legroom if available.

Anita: Exit rows are great but check seat recline and lapbelt extenders (some have non-reclinable walls). If you're tall, avoid middle of 3.

Maya: Ooh good point re: non-recline. Anyone use SeatGuru or similar? Link? :link:

Jonah: SeatGuru is my go-to. Example: https://seatguru.com/airlines/airline.php I always check for 'limited recline' notes.

Sam: My in-flight kit (tiny):
```
eye mask
noise-cancelling buds
inflatable neck pillow
pillowcase (clean)
aromatic balm
compression socks
light blanket / big scarf
phone charger + battery
``` 

Maya: Nice. Any airport layover tips? 2h vs 4h — worth leaving airport?

Anita: 2h stay put. 4h if you can do a quick city coffee + stretch. But factor in customs/immigration time. Always keep meds + essentials in carry-on.

Maya: Quick poll — which seat would you pick? :thumbsup: Aisle | :heart: Window | :eyes: Middle

(react below) :smile:

CheckinBot: Reminder: online check-in opens 24h before departure for most carriers — set a timer! (automated)

Sam: Also, pack earplugs & hydration. Avoid alcohol if you want to sleep.

Jonah: Pro tip: download offline maps + a white noise playlist.

Anita: If anyone's attending EuroConf — let's coordinate hotel shuttles in the other thread. :)
